elements.element: Customer has no contractual restriction on soliciting the other party's employees or personnel.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly prohibits both parties, including Customer, from directly soliciting certain employees of the other party.

elements.element: The non-solicitation covenant applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The covenant applies to “neither party” and also requires each party not to permit its affiliates to engage in the restricted solicitation.

elements.element: The prohibited conduct is limited to direct solicitation for employment.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is expressly limited to “directly solicit for employment.”

elements.element: The covered personnel are limited to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: The prohibition applies only to an employee “who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.”

elements.element: The restriction lasts no more than twelve months from the end of each relevant individual's involvement in the services.
elements.evidence: Although the clause refers to twelve months following the end of the individual's involvement, it also applies throughout the entire Agreement term. If involvement ends more than twelve months before the Agreement terminates, the restriction continues beyond the permitted twelve-month period.

elements.element: General advertisements and recruitment campaigns not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel are excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits general advertisements and recruitment campaigns not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by personnel are excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits hiring any person who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis.

elements.element: The covenant contains no prohibition on hiring.
elements.evidence: The clause states that it “does not prohibit either party from hiring any person,” and its operative restriction addresses solicitation rather than hiring.

result.reason: The operative language does not satisfy the preferred position because Customer remains bound by a non-solicit. It nearly implements the fallback, but the opening phrase applies the covenant throughout the Agreement term, so it can continue for more than twelve months after an individual's involvement ends. Because that duration element is not met, the fallback is not fully satisfied. The margin comment cannot cure the operative overbreadth.
